scope: Nine additional province-scale, one-sided local-food floors reconstructed from the Kamakura Great Land Registers. The records are retained as lower bounds only; the register method is not a saturation or global-scale target.

promotion_audit.decision: Farris (2006), Table 1.3 reports a rice-acreage-to-person conversion for each province. The unbracketed value is a documented locally supported rice-farming population floor; the bracketed +40% non-rice sensitivity is deliberately not treated as an uncertainty or capacity upper endpoint. Iwami and Hitachi have explicit omitted-paddy cautions and therefore remain conservative floors. Province boundaries are mapped with the Harvard CHGIS Tokugawa Japan GIS polygons and the corresponding EU5 historical-province selectors. No record supplies a saturation fraction or sets global scale.

records.label: Satsuma province, Kamakura Great Land Register local-food population floor
records.interval_semantics: Farris Table 1.3 converts 4,010 chō of registered rice fields using 0.181 chō per adult and a 16% child allowance, yielding 25,700 people. This is a rice-supported minimum, not a complete population or capacity interval.
pressure_evidence: Farris (2006), pp. 22-26 and Table 1.1, documents the Satsuma Great Land Register and compares register field totals with estate surveys.
Farris (2006), pp. 29-32 and Table 1.3, identifies food supply, grain shortages and famine as the principal demographic constraints and applies the same local rice-acreage conversion to Satsuma.
The lower endpoint is derived from locally registered rice acreage; non-rice fields and regional exchange are not silently counted.
shock_flags: register is dated 1190-1199; converted estimate is labelled circa 1280
records.food_regime: locally cultivated wet rice and dry fields, legumes, livestock and coastal fisheries
records.boundary_description: Medieval Satsuma province (Satsuma no kuni), represented by the documented CHGIS province polygon and the corresponding EU5 Satsuma province.
records.boundary_source: Harvard CHGIS Japan Historical GIS, Tokugawa Japan GIS 2004, jp_toku_kuni_pgn.shp, DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0
records.source_family_independence: This is one documentary source family shared with the other Farris province floors; it is not counted as an independent scale family.
records.notes: The retained value is the unbracketed rice-based floor; the bracketed 35,980 non-rice sensitivity is excluded from training.

records.label: Ōsumi province, Kamakura Great Land Register local-food population floor
records.interval_semantics: Farris Table 1.3 gives 19,336 people from the registered rice acreage under the rice-only conversion. It is a one-sided locally supported floor, not a total population estimate.
pressure_evidence: Farris (2006), pp. 22-26 and Tables 1.1-1.2, documents the register and estate-survey comparison.
Farris (2006), pp. 29-32, places the conversion in a food-limited demographic framework with famine and grain-shortage evidence.
Registered rice output alone supports the retained minimum; dry-field people and imports are not assumed.

records.boundary_description: Medieval Ōsumi province (Ōsumi no kuni), represented by the CHGIS province polygon and EU5 Ōsumi province selector.
records.boundary_source: Harvard CHGIS Japan Historical GIS, Tokugawa Japan GIS 2004, jp_toku_kuni_pgn.shp, DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0
records.source_family_independence: Shared Farris documentary source family; not an independent scale family.
records.notes: The +40% bracketed sensitivity (27,070) is not used as an upper label.

records.label: Iwami province, Kamakura Great Land Register conservative local-food floor
records.interval_semantics: Farris Table 1.3 reports 9,459 from Iwami's registered rice acreage. Farris warns that Iwami may have omitted rice land; therefore the number is retained only as a conservative one-sided floor and never as a point target.
pressure_evidence: Farris (2006), pp. 22-26 and Tables 1.1-1.2, documents the Iwami register and independent estate-survey corroboration.
Farris (2006), pp. 24-25 and 32-33, explicitly warns that Iwami's low result may omit rice land; this makes the recorded floor conservative rather than an upper capacity.
Farris (2006), pp. 29-32, places the reconstruction in a food-limited demographic context.
shock_flags: Japan Sea climate and demographic decline
possible omitted rice fields explicitly noted by Farris

records.label: Hitachi province, Kamakura Great Land Register conservative local-food floor
records.interval_semantics: Farris Table 1.3 reports 57,712 from Hitachi rice acreage. Farris warns that the register may record only shrine-contributing paddies; the retained value is consequently a conservative local-food floor, not a total or capacity interval.
pressure_evidence: Farris (2006), pp. 22-26 and Tables 1.1-1.2, documents Hitachi's register and independent survey corroboration.
Farris (2006), pp. 24-25 and 32-33, explicitly notes possible omitted paddies in Hitachi; no upward correction is used.
Farris (2006), pp. 29-32, links food availability and recurrent famine to population pressure.
